title: Lawrence Duhe's band and piccolo player Bab Frank
summary: Braud lists the Duhe band members and explains how Bab Frank played fiddle parts on piccolo.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, before you joined that, can you tell us some more about that band? You played with Roy Palmer and...

Well, Roy Palmer, that was Lewis, I mean, Lawrence Doey's band. Lil Hardin Armstrong on the piano, and Lawrence Doey on the clarinet, Sidney Bache clarinet, Bab Frank piccolo, and Sugar Johnny, cornet, and Toby Halls on the drum. That was a very fine organization, very, very good.
What kind of part did the Bab Frank play on the piccolo? I always wondered.
Well, he was very fine, very outstanding piccolo player.
Did he play something like the clarinet or a violin player?

Oh, no. He played fiddle parts on the piccolo. And he was a very fine piccolo player, because I can tell from some people that I met in the Georgia Ministrel Brass Band. He was once a member of that. Well, we call him Papa Teal here. That was Lorenzo Teal's father. He played clarinet in the band. And also, old man, Piku. He was a clarinet player in the Georgia Ministrel Band. That's way before my time, but I can remember fellas that just tell me, like, Fred Simpson, he was the leader of the band of New York. And he told me that those guys played with him. And they were very fine.
Or Bab Frank could read anything that was for the piccolo to read, and he played the fiddle parts on the piccolo.
And very fine. Did he play by ear?
